content.title: About
content.content: Brioche is a soft French bread made from wheat flour, eggs, butter, sugar and yeast. The dough is rich, slightly sweet, with a golden crust and a light, airy crumb. Brioche is often enjoyed at breakfast, as rolls, toast, or used in desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally brioche is shaped into a round loaf with a characteristic “crown” knot on top.
The original recipe uses a large amount of eggs, giving the bread its distinctive yellow hue.
Brioche is sometimes called the “royal bread” because it was served at French royal courts.
In the United States the “brioche bun” is popular for burgers and sandwiches.
Sweet versions may contain raisins, candied peel or chocolate chips.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Rich in carbohydrates and fats, brioche quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and yeast provide B1, B2, B3 and B6 vitamins important for metabolism.

items.title: Mineral content
items.content: Brioche supplies iron, magnesium and phosphorus, supporting blood and bone health.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: A modest amount of fiber from wheat flour aids normal digestion.

items.title: Mood improvement
items.content: Tryptophan from eggs can help synthesize serotonin, the “feel‑good” hormone.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Brioche is rich in fats and sugars, so it should be eaten in moderation, especially for weight management.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Traditional brioche contains wheat flour, making it unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweet varieties can raise blood sugar levels, which is important for diabetics to consider.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Eggs and butter add cholesterol, so those with high cholesterol should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Brioche can be enjoyed fresh, toasted with butter, used in sandwiches, as a base for French toast, in bread pudding, or served with jam, honey and cheese.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep brioche in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer storage freeze it in a bag – it will stay soft for up to 3 months. Thaw at room temperature or gently warm in the oven before serving.
